record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a replication of the original difference-in-means direction and directional ablation, reports refusal-rate results, and the file list includes result files.
record.gate_note: The README also reports layer-separation and token-attribution findings. It does not report results for the planned adversarial-suffix or multi-direction analyses. The activation-addition attempt is described as producing incoherent outputs, but no refusal rate for that attempt is given.
record.test_reason: The repo replicates Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction and directional ablation on Llama 3.2 3B Instruct. It reports refusal rates before and after ablation on AdvBench and JailbreakBench, the same kind of measure as the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors tentatively suggest the monotonic layer separation reflects a scale-dependent pattern. They caution it could be model-specific and needs cross-scale testing. They also report that harm-specific nouns rank as the top attributing tokens.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes difference-in-means direction extraction and directional ablation on Llama 3.2 3B Instruct, with AdvBench and JailbreakBench results. It adds token-attribution analysis; exact intervention details are not stated. This is a replication and extension repository.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported layer-separation pattern increases across layers and peaks at layer 27. Activation addition is reported as incoherent regardless of steering magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful/harmless separation increases monotonically across all 28 layers, peaking at layer 27 (26.76), unlike the middle-layer peak in larger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small models (3B), harmful/harmless separation along the refusal direction peaks at late layers rather than middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-3 tokens account for 56.1% of positive refusal-direction signal at layer 7; harm nouns rank highest. The authors state this is not causal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projection onto the refusal direction is concentrated on a few harm-specific prompt tokens.

record.problems: The README identifies a small harmful-prompt sample (128 AdvBench prompts), a single tested model, a brittle phrase-matching refusal scorer, and a token-attribution metric that does not establish causality. It reports no uncertainty estimates, no general-capability evaluation, and no category-specific ablation rates. Code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: None; all README-reported refusal-rate categories and relevant direction/attribution measurements were recorded. Results cited from Arditi et al. were not included as this repository's results.

untested.parts: Induction of refusal by activation addition (no refusal rate reported). Retention of other abilities under ablation (no capability evaluation). Other models.
All; adversarial suffixes are listed only as future work.
All; multi-direction analysis is listed only as future work.

record.verdict_notes: Informal GitHub replication on a single model. The README reports no uncertainty, no capability check, and no held-out split for AdvBench. The activation-addition failure is attributed by the authors to their hook placement, so it is not counted as evidence against V1's induction claim. The record's limits_scope label based on r3 is dropped.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports ablation results on two prompt sets and an activation-addition attempt, but does not establish that ablation was performed at every position, report addition-induced refusal rates, or test whether other abilities are largely intact. The activation-addition attempt produced incoherent outputs.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
The README proposes testing adversarial suffixes in future work; cited findings about other work are not this repository's results.
Multiple-direction analysis is listed as future work; the layer-separation result does not test whether refusal requires multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
